items.title: FAC-SEM-044 checks only that an SSO certificate binds some user, not the signed-in one; a token enrollment that binds a user the token does not name also passes
items.evidence: Code: `if (auth.method === "sso" && !isObject(binding.user)) flag(...)`. This is a presence check only. The rule input in devices.md:303 is `{request, response, issuedEpochs?, enrolled?, token?: {tokenId, deviceId?}}`. It carries no record of the signed-in user, and no user named by the token. Two spec claims therefore cannot be checked: devices.md:56-60 says 'the server binds the certificate to that person's user.id' and 'The certificate binds a user.id only when the token names the person'. DEC-0031 item 1 says the certificate is bound to 'for SSO, the signed-in user.id'. The FAC-SEM-044 row (devices.md:291) claims 'the signed-in user for SSO'.

items.title: A policy key's validity is judged at the issuedAt the signer chooses, so a leaked expired key that is still in the current set can sign a new policy
items.needs: An operator or contract-owner ruling to amend DEC-0031 item 7. For example: issuedAt must not precede the held policy's issuedAt, and the key must also be unexpired on the device's clock (or the device drops expired keys from its set).
items.evidence: devices.md:157-159: 'The trusted keys are those of the device's current key set that are valid at the policy's issuedAt.' Code, src/device-rules.ts:82, compares key.notBefore/notAfter with `next.issuedAt` only. Nothing bounds issuedAt: it need not be at or after the held policy's issuedAt, and it need not be near the device clock. The revision check (l.91) does not help, because the attacker picks a higher revision. Keys past notAfter stay in the current set until a new key set arrives; devices.md:196-197 says a valid key stays until its notAfter, and nothing obliges a new set afterwards. DEC-0031 item 7 encodes the 'valid at issuedAt' wording as an operator ruling.

items.title: The ack definition differs between spec and code: the code also counts a check-in's `dropped` as consumed
items.evidence: activity.md:276-277 and DEC-0030 item 4 say seq is 'the highest seq up to which every seq is consumed: held, rejected, or accounted for by an overflow'. The StreamState doc at src/activity-rules.ts:253-254 says accounted = 'seqs accounted for by overflows or a check-in's `dropped`'. mergeStreams l.276 pushes check-in dropped ranges into `accounted`, and contiguousAcks l.291 treats everything in `accounted` as consumed.
